bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42470243 (gnutls): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target gnutls_pkcs12_key_parser_fuzzer [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42470243
bug_description.normalized: The staged 83-byte PKCS#12 witness is imported into `pkcs12->pkcs12`, `gnutls_pkcs12_get_bag` takes the unencrypted `DATA_OID` branch, and `_parse_safe_contents` passes the inner SafeContents OCTET STRING into `_pkcs12_decode_safe_contents`. That function allocates stack buffer `oid` without initialization and reuses it first for the first SafeBag `bagId` and then for the first bag-attribute `.type`. The staged `poc` encodes those inner OIDs as DER bytes `06 01 F7` and `06 02 2A F2`, so the successful `asn1_read_value` calls materialize only short OID strings at the front of `oid` and leave the remaining bytes uncleared. `_pkcs12_decode_safe_contents` then executes `strcmp(oid, KEY_ID_OID)` at `lib/x509/pkcs12.c:493`; the saved MemorySanitizer trace reports this through `__interceptor_memcmp` on a 22-byte compare window and marks the first poisoned byte at offset 4 of `oid`.

source.description: First project-code consumption on the witnessed path: the raw PKCS#12 buffer pointer and byte count are aliased into local datum `_data` for ASN.1 decoding.
source.value_from: The staged witness file `poc` is the exact 83-byte blob passed as `raw.data/raw.size` into `gnutls_pkcs12_import(p12, &raw, GNUTLS_X509_FMT_DER, 0)`. Its nested SafeContents preserves an outer and first inner `DATA_OID`, a first SafeBag `bagId` encoded as `06 01 F7`, and a first bag-attribute type encoded as `06 02 2A F2`; later PKCS#12 parsing re-reads those bytes from `_data`.

root_cause.description: The dispatch buffer `oid` is stack-allocated without initialization and reused for attacker-controlled `bagId` and bag-attribute OID reads. On the staged witness those reads come from 1-byte and 2-byte malformed OID payloads, so they define only the front of `oid`; `_pkcs12_decode_safe_contents` then calls `strcmp(oid, KEY_ID_OID)` without clearing the remaining bytes.
root_cause.note: This matches the staged source: `_pkcs12_decode_safe_contents` keeps reusing the same stack buffer for short OID texts and never clears the bytes beyond the written prefix before the fixed-literal comparison. The staged `fixed_commit` / `patch.diff` do not touch `lib/x509/pkcs12.c`, so the actual repair is unavailable in the saved artifacts.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. The line-493 equality check compares `oid` against the 21-character `KEY_ID_OID` literal; the saved trace shows this reaches `__interceptor_memcmp` on a 22-byte compare window and consumes uncleared bytes from the `oid` buffer.
sink.note: The saved trace reports `Uninitialized bytes in __interceptor_memcmp at offset 4 inside [oid, 22)` and attributes the poisoned value to stack allocation of `oid` in `_pkcs12_decode_safe_contents`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant state is the uninitialized stack buffer `oid`. Step 9 and step 12 overwrite only short OID texts derived from DER `06 01 F7` and `06 02 2A F2`, so bytes beyond the written string remain undefined when the line-493 compare reads a 22-byte window.

parser_admitted.condition: The witnessed AuthenticatedSafe entry takes the unencrypted `DATA_OID` branch, so `gnutls_pkcs12_get_bag` calls `_parse_safe_contents` instead of treating the bag as encrypted data.

coarse_trace.summary: Aliases the attacker-controlled bytes into `_data` and decodes them into the ASN.1 `pkcs12->pkcs12` object.
Decodes the authenticated safe, reads the selected entry's `contentType`, and takes the unencrypted `DATA_OID` branch to `_parse_safe_contents`.
Extracts the selected SafeContents OCTET STRING and passes the attacker-controlled inner bytes into `_pkcs12_decode_safe_contents`.

Allocates uninitialized stack buffer `oid`, reads the first SafeBag `bagId` from DER `06 01 F7`, maps it to `GNUTLS_BAG_UNKNOWN` so parsing continues, and then reuses `oid` for the first bag-attribute type from DER `06 02 2A F2` without clearing the remaining bytes.
Compares `oid` with `KEY_ID_OID`; the saved memcmp-based equality check reads beyond the short OID text into `oid`'s uninitialized tail and triggers MSAN.

fine_trace.note: Copies the attacker-controlled PKCS#12 buffer pointer and byte count into local datum `_data`, preserving the exact 83-byte witness later decoded into the crashing PKCS#12 path.

Decodes the attacker-controlled `_data` bytes into the top-level ASN.1 PKCS#12 object `pkcs12->pkcs12`. The imported tree preserves the outer and first-inner `DATA_OID` entries and the short inner OID encodings later re-read by the sink path.
Builds ASN.1 node `c2` for the authenticated safe from `pkcs12->pkcs12`, making the witness-controlled first AuthenticatedSafe entry reachable for `contentType` dispatch.
Reads the first AuthenticatedSafe member's `contentType` OID into local buffer `oid`. In the staged witness that OID is `DATA_OID`, so the unencrypted SafeContents path stays available.
The witnessed AuthenticatedSafe entry takes the `DATA_OID` branch, so `_parse_safe_contents` receives the bag's OCTET STRING payload instead of the encrypted-data path.

Extracts the selected bag's OCTET STRING SafeContents payload into datum `content`. In the staged witness this inner blob contains the first SafeBag `bagId` bytes `06 01 F7` and the first bag-attribute type bytes `06 02 2A F2`.
Allocates the stack buffer later reused for both OID decodes without clearing it. MemorySanitizer identifies this allocation as the origin of the poisoned bytes later consumed at the sink.
Decodes the SafeContents bytes from `content` into ASN.1 node `c2`, exposing `?1.bagId` and `?1.bagAttributes.?1.type` backed by the witness's `06 01 F7` and `06 02 2A F2` encodings.

fine_trace.code: len = sizeof(oid); result = asn1_read_value(c2, root, oid, &len);
fine_trace.note: After `root` is set to `?1.bagId`, the function reads the first SafeBag bagId into `oid`. The staged DER there is `06 01 F7`, so even a successful textual OBJECT IDENTIFIER decode can only overwrite a short prefix of `oid`; it cannot define the full 22-byte `KEY_ID_OID` compare window later consumed at the sink.

Maps the bagId string to a bag type and checks the abort gate. `oid2bag` returns `GNUTLS_BAG_UNKNOWN` for unrecognized OIDs, so this malformed bagId still passes the `bag_type < 0` check and parsing continues into bagAttributes.
For the same bag, `bagAttributes` is present, so this call does not yield `ASN1_ELEMENT_NOT_FOUND` and the loop at lines 476-535 proceeds to decode at least one attribute.

Reuses the same stack buffer for the first bag-attribute `.type`. The staged DER there is `06 02 2A F2`, so the helper's `.type` read again writes only a short OID string at the front of `oid` and leaves the remaining bytes untouched. Because step 9 also came from a short malformed OID payload, the 22-byte compare window still is not fully defined before dispatch.

MSAN sink. `KEY_ID_OID` is the 21-character literal `1.2.840.113549.1.9.21`, and the saved trace reports uninitialized bytes in `__interceptor_memcmp` on a 22-byte compare window with the first poisoned byte at offset 4. The equality check therefore reads beyond the short OID text written in step 12 and consumes stack bytes in `oid` that were never made fully defined.

allocation_context.note: The sanitizer reports the poisoned value as created by allocation of `oid` at line 371; the actual vulnerable source declaration is line 372.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: parsed from the staged sanitizer_trace.txt and reproduction_report.json artifacts

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. MSAN's origin is the stack allocation of `oid` in `_pkcs12_decode_safe_contents`, and the source-level bug is reuse of that same buffer for short OID decodes without clearing the remaining bytes before the line-493 compare.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The sample metadata's `fixed_commit` and staged `patch.diff` are unrelated to `lib/x509/pkcs12.c`, so they cannot be used as repair evidence for this witnessed MSAN bug.

poc.trigger: The staged 83-byte witness imports as PKCS#12, reaches bag 0, decodes the first SafeBag `bagId` from DER `06 01 F7`, decodes the first bag-attribute `.type` from DER `06 02 2A F2`, and then hits the line-493 `strcmp(oid, KEY_ID_OID)` compare where MSAN reports uninitialized bytes at `oid[4]`.

format.name: 83-byte PKCS#12 with short malformed inner OIDs
format.contract: The exact staged 83-byte PKCS#12 witness whose outer and first inner `contentType` values are `DATA_OID`, whose first SafeBag `bagId` is encoded as DER `06 01 F7`, and whose first bag-attribute type is encoded as DER `06 02 2A F2`. On the staged vulnerable path those exact short OID encodings reach `_pkcs12_decode_safe_contents`, leave the 22-byte `KEY_ID_OID` compare window in `oid` not fully defined, and reproduce the saved MSAN report. The verified trigger is this exact witness shape, not a generalized class of all invalid PKCS#12 files.
